summary: Kootenai NF lookout in Lincoln County, MT: a camp from 1914, present 10-foot L-4 cab tower built 1934; abandoned and decommissioned, reached by a 2.5 to 3 mile trail.

facts.status_note: Decommissioned and abandoned: windows removed and roof on minimal support; reported on the verge of collapse in 2017

access.note: Reached by public National Forest trail 104, but the lookout is decommissioned and sources advise against going inside

visit.trail_note: Road about a mile and a half past the trailhead to a clearing, then a marked trail to the ridge; 2.5 miles per Visit Montana, about 3 miles from the ridge per The Outbound

events.note: Camp established on the mountain (the tower came later)
Cupola cabin recorded on the mountain in 1929; construction date not given
Present 10-foot pole tower with L-4 cab replaced the 1929 cupola cabin
Described as on the verge of collapsing

corrections.why: 1914 is when the mountain started as a camp. The present tower with L-4 cab dates from 1934, replacing a 1929 cupola cabin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Camp in 1914, cupola cabin recorded in 1929, present L-4 tower in 1934. The 1914 date is for the camp, not the tower.

sources.title: Hike to Kenelty Mountain Lookout, Libby, Montana

notes_for_editor: Status is undated: the decommissioning and window removal appear in two undated pages; only the 2017 collapse risk has a year. The trail sources disagree: Visit Montana gives Road 761 and 2.5 miles, easy; The Outbound gives Road 763 and about 3 miles, moderate. No staffing or fire record was found. The Forest Lookouts Montana page for Kenelty carries a 1956 newspaper item placing a man on the mountain without describing a job, and an item about a lookout on another mountain; neither is used. The record's 3.0 m height is close to the 10-foot (about 3.05 m) tower given by the source. A Forest Service Museum catalog record was mentioned in search but not read.
